turns.user:
Hey. Okay, so here's the one that keeps coming back.

I'm on a commuter train at night — the kind I take home from work. I realize I've missed my stop. The train just keeps going, past all the stations, and then it turns off into this dark tunnel that isn't on any map. The lights inside flicker and dim, and it gets cold. I'm the only one left in the car. I try to stand up to get to the door, but my legs feel heavy, like the floor is pulling me down. Then I wake up with my heart racing.

It happens maybe once a week, and it's been going on for a few months now. I usually wake up pretty anxious and can't get back to sleep for a while.
turns.reply:
That sounds unsettling. You’ve told me what happens and how you feel when you wake up.

Is there anything else about the dream that feels important to you?

turns.user:
Yeah, there's one thing. The tunnel entrance is the part that gets me most. It's this perfectly round black opening in the rock, and the train just glides into it like it's supposed to be there. There's no sound once we're inside — the usual track noise just stops. And there's a feeling of being taken somewhere I didn't agree to go.

Also — I can never tell what time it is in the dream. My phone doesn't work in the tunnel. No signal, no clock. That sense of losing track of time is part of what makes it so unsettling, I think.
turns.reply:
That tunnel entrance does sound especially disturbing. You’ve told me what happens and how you feel.

Would you like to start rewriting this dream now?
